new_entities.name: Sodium bicarbonate supplementation
new_entities.description: Oral sodium bicarbonate used to increase extracellular buffering capacity before high-intensity exercise.

new_entities.name: High-intensity anaerobic performance
new_entities.description: Performance during repeated short-duration high-intensity efforts that rely heavily on anaerobic energy production.

edges.effect_quant: The most consistent benefit appears in repeated rather than single anaerobic efforts. In one meta-analysis, sodium bicarbonate improved mean power in repeated Wingate tests with SMDs ranging from 0.09 to 0.62, and direct athlete trials report about 2.9 to 5.9% gains in repeated-bout work output.
edges.population: trained athletes performing repeated high-intensity anaerobic efforts
edges.mechanism: Sodium bicarbonate raises extracellular bicarbonate and helps buffer the hydrogen ions that accumulate during repeated maximal work. That does not guarantee better performance in a single all-out sprint, but it can preserve output when fatigue and acidosis build over successive bouts.
edges.summary: This is a legitimate ergogenic edge, but it is more specific than the hype often suggests. Sodium bicarbonate tends to help repeated Wingate-style or sport-specific high-intensity efforts more than a single short sprint, which is why the best-supporting trials are the ones that stress repeated-bout fatigue.
edges.caveats: Gastrointestinal side effects are common and can erase the benefit in practice. The response is also protocol-dependent, so single-bout laboratory tests may underestimate the scenarios where bicarbonate actually helps.

evidence.citation: GrgicJ et al 2022 J Am Nutr Assoc
evidence.notes: Effects of Sodium Bicarbonate Ingestion on Measures of Wingate Test Performance: A Meta-Analysis.
